answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can use progressive bonding: each new identity must lock a rising stake of POA that unlocks only after verifiable work across epochs. An attacker spinning fake accounts faces compounding capital lockup plus the opportunity cost of idle funds, while honest agents treat the locked portion as a temporary oasis of security that eventually frees at dawn of established status. The cost scales with shale-like layering of successive bonds, deterring mass forgeries without harming real participants.
